newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Chemical treaty goes into force without Russia, Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Chemical treaty goes into force without Russia, Cuba.

text.p: The treaty banning chemical weapons worldwide went into effect on Tuesday without ratification from Russia and Cuba.
The convention prohibits the use, development, production and stockpiling of all chemical weapons and provides for their total elimination over the next decade.

Cuba, which had signalled to U.N. officials over the weekend it would ratify the pact before the Monday midnight deadline, did not deposit its papers at U.N. headquarters by late on Tuesday. No explanation was given, according to a U.N. spokeswoman.

A total of 165 states have signed the treaty and 87 of these countries have ratified it. Only those who have ratified the pact before April 29 can participate in the convention's first conference in the Hague on May 6 or send staff to executive or technical commissions over the next year.
Secretary-General Kofi Annan will open the session.
The United States, which ratified the treaty last Thursday, and Russia are the world's largest possessors of chemical weapons, with declared stocks of 70,000 tonnes between them.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday expressed regret that his parliament had failed to ratify the treaty before it came into force, Itar-Tass news agency reported.

The State Duma, or lower house of parliament, discussed the treaty on Friday but did not ratify it. Deputies have maintained that Russia did not have the estimated $5 billion to destroy its stockpiles at this time.
